blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Kolkata Metro, operational since 1984, is India's first metro railway system and functions as a full railway zone.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (Kolkata) is the oldest operating port in India and the country's premier riverine port.
National Waterway 1 (NW-1) spans the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system connecting Haldia to Prayagraj.
Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport (Dum Dum) and Bagdogra Airport form the primary air transit backbone of West Bengal.
The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) terminates at Dankuni in West Bengal, significantly boosting industrial logistics.
Kolkata Metro is recognized as the 17th Railway Zone of Indian Railways, unlike other municipal metro systems in India.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port is a riverine port situated on the Hooghly River, dependent on water discharge from the Farakka Barrage for navigability.
National Waterway 1 (NW-1) is the longest inland waterway in India, originating at Haldia in West Bengal.
